title: Give (or take back) Invardia support access to a PIM Manager installation
purpose: Gives (or with -Remove takes back) the customer's Invardia Support app its access to this PIM Manager installation: troubleshoot = a read-only contained SQL user; setup = member of the SQL admin group and owner of PIM's own app registrations and groups. Every change is read back.
whenToRun: When the customer wants Invardia support to look at (troubleshoot) or repair (setup) their installation, and to take that access back afterwards (-Remove). The guided public install runs it for you when a support app is named. For a private installation, run it from inside the network (the SQL server has no public endpoint). It is part of the PIM Manager release package, not a separate download: run it from the package folder that Install-Invardia (or the guided install) downloaded and verified (.\tools\setup\Grant-PimSupportAccess.ps1). Invardia's New-InvardiaSupportApp.ps1 must have created the support app in the tenant first.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: The SQL admin group is role-assignable: adding or removing a member needs this role. Without it that part is reported and the rest continues (exit 1).

runAs.name: Owner of PIM's app registrations and groups (or Application Administrator / Groups Administrator)
runAs.scope: PIM's own objects in the tenant (only for -Level setup / -Remove)
runAs.why: Adds or removes the support app as an owner of the Manager's sign-in app, the access request API app, the Manager members group and the SQL admin group.

runAs.name: Member of the environment's SQL admin group (grp-pim-sql-admins) or the server's Entra admin, signed in through the browser or the Invardia Support app session (no Azure CLI)
runAs.scope: the environment's SQL database (only for -Level troubleshoot / -Remove)
runAs.why: Creates or drops the support app's contained database user.

runAs.name: Reader
runAs.scope: the PIM resource group (only when -SqlServer is not given)
runAs.why: Finds the PIM SQL server in -ResourceGroup.

changes.object: contained user [invardia-support] created from the support app's SID (never FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER)
changes.permission: db_datareader + VIEW DEFINITION (db_datawriter, db_ddladmin and db_owner are revoked if it had them)
changes.why: -Level troubleshoot: Invardia can read the store and its schema, nothing else.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (drops the user).

changes.object: the support app's service principal as a member of the SQL admin group (members/$ref)
changes.permission: member of grp-pim-sql-admins (the SQL server's admin group)
changes.why: -Level setup: Invardia can create users, deploy the schema and repair the store.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (takes back the membership).

changes.object: the support app's service principal as an owner (owners/$ref) of the Manager's sign-in app, the access request API app, the Manager members group and the SQL admin group
changes.scope: PIM's own app registrations and groups only
changes.why: -Level setup: the support app's Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy is then enough to repair PIM's own objects later, without a tenant-wide right.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (takes back every ownership).

changes.target: Microsoft Entra ID and the SQL database
changes.object: the membership, the ownerships and the contained user (only with -Remove)

parameters.name: AppId
parameters.help: The Invardia Support app's application (client) id in this tenant.

parameters.name: Level
parameters.help: troubleshoot (read-only SQL user) or setup (SQL admin group member + owner of PIM's objects).

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id. Every token is pinned to it.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The PIM subscription (used to find the SQL server when -SqlServer is not given).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The PIM resource group (used to find the SQL server when -SqlServer is not given).

parameters.name: EnvLabel
parameters.help: The per-environment label the deploy used (-EnvLabel), so the right app registrations and groups are found.

parameters.name: Remove
parameters.help: Take back BOTH levels: the membership, the ownerships and the contained user.

readsOnly: the support app's service principal, PIM's app registrations and groups and their owners / members (Microsoft Graph)
the SQL servers in -ResourceGroup (only when -SqlServer is not given)
network: management.azure.com (only to find the SQL server)
whatIf: Reads the support app and PIM's objects and prints 'What if: Performing the operation "add owner" / "add member" / "contained user [invardia-support] (db_datareader + VIEW DEFINITION)" on target ...' for every change it would make, then 'preview only -- nothing was changed'. Nothing is written.
undo: Run the script again with -Remove: it drops the contained user and takes back the membership and every ownership.
